tests_cover: density volume scales as coordinate scale to the number of dimensions
great circle distance handles antimeridian and identical points
within-taxon prediction detects strong synthetic environmental information
insufficient prediction sample size is not admitted
limitations: This is a 50-observation, 30-rarefaction, 512-Monte-Carlo-draw feasibility pilot, not a final density estimate.
Taxon-bootstrap intervals are pointwise and not multiplicity-corrected; phylogenetic and spatial dependence across taxa remain.
Environmental and geographic breadth describe sampled records, not independently estimated range area or niche breadth.
Geographic breadth is RMS great-circle separation, not occupied area.
Environment breadth is RMS distance across four standardized correlated exposures, not environment hypervolume.
Image resampling standardizes count but does not remove observer, spatial, photographic or measurement bias.
Shared smoothing can dominate very narrow distributions; bandwidth and density-Monte-Carlo stability are not yet evaluated.
Involucre and whole-capitulum projection volumes are descriptive only and discard substantial variance.
Five-degree cell holdout has no spatial buffer, uses one fold assignment, and does not test seasonality or independent validation.
Prediction operates in coordinates calibrated on all trait observations, not nested training-only coordinate estimation.
Negative held-out gain is retained, including severe degradation in some taxa.
Overlap and Wasserstein analyses are not yet implemented in this pilot.
